name: awk

source.upstream: onetrueawk/awk (Brian Kernighan's reference AWK; the same lineage NetBSD and many BSDs ship as their system awk)
source.license: Lucent Technologies 1997 permissive license; see LICENSE

generated_files.note: Vendored as a pristine generated file rather than regenerated at build time, matching shell/toybox/crt/generated/*.h's own convention -- this project's CMake build has no bison/yacc dependency otherwise. Regenerate only if awkgram.y itself changes.

generated_files.generated_by: maketab.c, compiled and run as a native host tool (this project's own crt-cc, targeting the same host the build runs on) against awkgram.tab.h: `./maketab awkgram.tab.h > proctab.c`
generated_files.note: maketab.c itself is kept in src/ for reference/reproducibility but is NOT part of the crt_awk build -- only its one-time output (proctab.c) is compiled.

notes: Imported to give this project's own rootfs (mksh + toybox + this) a real AWK, matching why mksh/toybox exist at all: bare Windows has none, and most autoconf-generated configure scripts require one.

Chosen over enabling toybox's own toys/pending/awk.c: that implementation is disabled by default even in Bionic's own upstream toybox config (CFG_AWK 0), signaling real incompleteness; onetrueawk is small, POSIX-focused, and is what NetBSD/many BSDs ship as their actual system awk.

Deliberately NOT solved by pointing configure at a host-installed awk (e.g. Git for Windows' bundled gawk.exe): that would be an uncontrolled, per-developer-machine dependency linked against a different runtime (MSYS), breaking the same reproducibility/self-containment principle that motivated building mksh/toybox against this project's own CRT in the first place. Linux/macOS need no such workaround since the OS itself always provides a real awk; only Windows needed one built.

One adaptation to upstream source: src/parse.c's ptoi()/itonp() helpers (smuggling a small int through a bison-stack Node* slot, never a real pointer dereference) cast through `long`, which truncates on Windows LLP64 (32-bit long, 64-bit pointers); changed to `intptr_t`. See the inline comment at the change site.

Filled real, general (not awk-specific) CRT/libm gaps found compiling this: atan2()/atan() (libm/src/freebsd/e_atan2.c, s_atan.c, both from FreeBSD msun -- NOT libc/src/regex/'s NetBSD-regex import, a separate upstream), system() (libc/src/process.c), rand()/srand()/random()/srandom() (libc/src/random.c), SIGFPE si_code FPE_* constants (include/signal.h), and <stdnoreturn.h> (missing entirely before this).

Running real awk programs (not just compiling awk) surfaced a real, general printf/snprintf bug unrelated to awk itself: %g with an explicit precision (e.g. the %.30g get_str_val()/tran.c always uses for integral numbers) zero-padded the rendered digit string a second time instead of leaving it alone (format_double_general()/format_long_double_general() in libc/src/printf.c were not clearing spec->precision_set before their final write_formatted() call, unlike their fixed-point/exponential siblings). Fixed, with regression coverage added to tests/printf_test.c.
